title: [D6 Orchestration] Deterministic routing and the escalation branch
summary: `helena.orchestration` is no longer a placeholder: `route(escalation, outcome)` is `concept/03`'s routing `if` transcribed — deterministic escalation first with `deterministic_signal`, then triage not-`normal` with `triage_suspicious`, else `None` for finish — and `assess(...)` is the deterministic code around it, computing the escalation from the projection BEFORE the triage call, running triage, routing, and deriving the analyst request (emitter, trigger, prompt version, budgets; the context, its version and the rendering unchanged) when a branch fires. `Assessment` is the in-process record it returns: the triage request, the `Escalation`, the triage outcome, the trigger, the analyst request, the `Analysis`, and one disclosure ledger per stage. Two structured log records make the routing countable and its ORDER observable.
assumption_validated: That 'no model output determines control flow' can be demonstrated by execution rather than asserted about the source, and that the escalation-before-triage ordering can be too. Both held. The same escalating context triaged four ways (`normal`, `suspicious`, an unparseable answer that becomes a typed failure, and an endpoint that never answers) routes identically to the analyst under `deterministic_signal`, and the whole `Escalation` object compares equal across those runs. The ordering is read out of ONE shared log stream — the router and both model clients write to it, so `orchestration.escalation_evaluated` preceding the first `agents.model.call` is an observation of the run rather than a claim about the file. Over real data: a real capture, a real ThreatFox extract through the real loader, the mapping view's own confidence and `port_matched`, and the committed thresholds produce an escalation that runs the analyst over a model saying `normal`. A negative result worth recording: the two prompt versions are BOTH `v1` (a prompt version is per-package), so the derived analyst request's `versions` compares EQUAL to the triage request's today — a stored row tells the two prompts apart by the emitter, not by `prompt_version` alone.
makes_buildable: Task 43 (assessment persistence) gets the exact object to store and every field it needs already assembled and validated: `Assessment.request` (tenant, sensor, host, window, context reference and version, the version set), `.escalation` (policy_version, thresholds_version, evidence_ids, claims_read, candidates, gaps), `.triage` and `.analysis.outcome` (the `AgentResult`/`AgentFailure` pair with citations, gaps, retrieval trace and `cost`), `.analysis.decision` (the constrained verdict), `.analysis.retrievals`, `.trigger` and `.analyst_request` (why analysis ran, under which budgets and prompt), and the two `Disclosures` ledgers keyed by emitter. `Assessment.terminal` is which of the two outcomes is the verdict, for D7's one-message-per-terminal-outcome rule. Task 44 (ephemeral state and re-run) gets the half that is already true — `helena.orchestration` holds no mutable module-level object at all, asserted — and the key its re-run is defined on is `(context_id, context_version, trigger)`, all three of which are on this object. Task 45 (assessment replay) gets a runner whose only non-deterministic inputs are the two model clients and the provider tools; constructing the tools with `replay=True` (task 41) is the whole of the provider half.

verification.detail: 1609 passed, 1 skipped in 599s on the final tree. Full suite against the real migrated engine, run three times: a baseline before any change (1578 passed, 1 skipped), one mid-work, and this one after the last edit. tests/test_orchestration.py went from 1 placeholder test to 32 collected (27 functions, one parametrized over the six-row routing table), of which 3 are engine-backed: a real capture normalized through the real ingest path, a real ThreatFox extract loaded through `load_threatfox`, the real renderer, and the routing decision the store's own numbers produce. The one skip is a pre-existing CONDITIONAL live-model skip (tests/test_analyst.py:1724) whose count varies run to run with what the configured endpoint answers — it was 1 in the baseline, 2 mid-work and 1 here, and none of the three is new.

deferred: BUILDING THE TRIAGE REQUEST FROM THE STORE. `concept/03` puts 'renders agent input' in Orchestration and this increment does not do it: the caller passes the triage request in, and `analyst_request` derives the analyst's from it. The reason is that nothing in the tree reads a context's `enrichment_snapshot_version`, `normalization_snapshot_version` or `aggregation_version` out of the engine, so a request assembled here would have to INVENT three recorded versions — `concept/instruction.md` §4's 'do not infer a behaviour you could test', applied to a provenance field. THIS IS AN UNOWNED GAP: no remaining D6 task (43 persistence, 44 ephemeral state, 45 replay) lists it, and task 52's end-to-end run is the first thing that cannot proceed without it. `helena.rendering.RenderingStore.project` + `helena.rendering.v1.render` + `helena.hosts.load()` are the three pieces that exist; the missing one is which snapshot versions a context's claims came from.

PERSISTING ANYTHING. `Assessment` is in-process. No assessment table, no citation join rows, no gaps table, no retrieval-trace or disclosure rows — task 43 owes all of them, and every claim here about replay is a claim about a shape being ready rather than a property that holds.
EMITTING ANYTHING. `Assessment.terminal` is which outcome is the verdict and nothing consumes it; the sink and the output topic are D7 (tasks 46-47).

RE-RUN RECOVERY, keyed by (context reference, context version, trigger). Task 44. What is true today is only the absence half: the module holds no mutable module-level state, so nothing of one context's run survives into the next.

A ROUTER THAT LOOPS OVER CONTEXTS. `assess` is one context, which is `concept/03`'s 'an assessment is one function call over one versioned context snapshot'. What drives it over a stream of contexts does not exist and was not invented here.

PACING, RATE LIMITS AND THE THRESHOLD'S CALIBRATION. Unchanged from tasks 36-39 and ADR-0023 §7: 0.80 is a measured position in a feed's distribution, not a measured escalation rate, and there is no labelled corpus. This increment routes on it; it does not evaluate it.
lessons: THE ORDERING CLAIM 'ESCALATION IS COMPUTED BEFORE TRIAGE' IS TESTABLE BY EXECUTION, AND THE MECHANISM IS THE LOG STREAM. `helena.observability.StructuredLogger` takes a stream, and `helena.agents.ModelClient` takes a logger — so handing the router and both model clients ONE `io.StringIO` makes the order of the lines the order the code ran in. `orchestration.escalation_evaluated` before the first `agents.model.call` is then an observation rather than an assertion about the source. Reusable by anything else in this tree that has an ordering invariant between a deterministic step and a model call.

THE TWO PROMPT VERSIONS COLLIDE AT `v1`, AND A STORED ROW NEEDS THE EMITTER TO TELL THEM APART. `triage.version('v1')` and `analyst.version('v1')` both report `v1` because a prompt version is per-package. A test asserting that the derived analyst request differs from the triage request in `versions` FAILS today for that reason, and the honest test is a subset assertion plus a note. Anything that reconstructs a prompt from a stored `prompt_version` must key on (emitter, prompt_version), never on the version alone.

`model_copy(update=...)` DOES NOT RE-VALIDATE IN PYDANTIC v2, so deriving a contract object with it produces the one instance in the system the contract never checked. `analyst_request` rebuilds through `AgentRequest(**fields)` instead, which is what makes `AgentRequest`'s own emitter/trigger pairing check and its triage-budget refusal apply to the derived request too.

AN ANALYST RUN WITH `provider_tools=()` MAKES EXACTLY ONE MODEL CALL AND NEVER ENTERS THE LOOP (`helena.analyst._retrieve` returns immediately on empty declarations). That is what lets a routing test be a routing test: 24 of the 27 tests here need no engine at all, because a routing assertion needs an analyst that RAN, not one that retrieved.

THE LOG RECORD'S FIELDS ARE NOT AT THE TOP LEVEL. `helena.observability.StructuredLogger._emit` lifts `event`, `context_id`, `event_id` and `versions` out and puts everything else under `fields`. A test reading a log line has to unwrap once; three tests here go through one helper for it.
failed_approaches: Grouping the twelve wiring arguments of `assess` into a frozen `Pipeline` dataclass was designed and dropped before it was written. It reads better at the call site and it is a container that exists for exactly one caller — `concept/instruction.md` §1's 'do not add a parameter, a registry or a plugin point for a second case that does not exist'. The flat keyword-argument signature makes every input the router depends on visible where it is called, which for the component whose whole job is 'no hidden control flow' is a feature rather than a cost. If tasks 43-45 each end up rebuilding the same twelve values, that is the second and third caller and the struct becomes justified then.

Asserting the escalation-before-triage ordering off the AST (statement index of the `escalate` call versus the `triage.run` call) was written and replaced by the log-stream test. An ordering claim asserted by reading the source is a claim about the source; the shared stream is the execution. The AST test that REMAINED is a different claim — that `route` calls only `triage.escalates` and reads only `escalation.escalates` — which is about what the code may not contain rather than about what it did.

Letting `assess` load `thresholds`, `budget_policy`, `send_policy`, `inherit` and `retry` from their config files as defaults was considered and rejected: file I/O per context, and a run scored against a policy it never ran under. They are required keyword arguments; the RULES are the exception and are loaded from the `policy_version` the request records, exactly as `helena.analyst.run` loads the composition rule.

One disclosure ledger shared by both stages was considered and rejected: `helena.disclosure.Disclosures` records the emitter it is the ledger of, so a shared one would file the analyst's disclosures under triage. `assess` builds one per run from that run's own request and returns both.
next_session_should_know: Task 43 is assessment persistence and it stores what this task assembles. EIGHT THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE ENTRY POINT IS `orchestration.assess(triage_request, *, projection, triage_client, analyst_client, retry, triage_prompt, analyst_prompt, provider_tools, thresholds, budget_policy, send_policy, inherit, logger) -> Assessment`. It raises `OrchestrationError` only for a request that is not a triage request; everything a model, an endpoint or a provider did comes back as a typed outcome on the `Assessment`. (2) `Assessment` HAS EIGHT FIELDS AND TWO INVARIANTS IT ENFORCES: `analyst_request`, `analysis` and `analyst_disclosures` are non-`None` EXACTLY where `trigger` is, and `analyst_request.trigger` must equal `trigger`. `Assessment.terminal` is the analyst's outcome if analysis ran and triage's otherwise — that is `concept/03`'s 'one message per terminal outcome', and D7 reads it. (3) THE ROUTER IS `route(escalation, outcome) -> str | None` AND IT IS PURE. `None` means finish; there is no `FINISH` sentinel because a constant equal to `None` is a config key with one value. `orchestration.FINISHED` is the WORD the log line uses for that branch, not a return value. (4) THE TRIGGER IS ALREADY A CONTRACT FIELD and this is its first writer. `analyst_request(request, trigger=, prompt_version=, granted=)` changes emitter, trigger, budgets and prompt version and NOTHING else — same context id, same context version, same rendering object — so the triage row and the analyst row join on one snapshot. (5) THE ANALYST'S BUDGET COMES FROM `config/policy.toml` VIA `budget_policy.for_emitter('analyst')`, never from the triage request. (6) TWO LOG EVENTS, `orchestration.escalation_evaluated` and `orchestration.routed`, and they are deliberately two: one shared record would make 'escalated, and triage also said suspicious' indistinguishable from 'escalated, and triage said normal', which is the case the whole deterministic input exists for. `routed.triage_outcome` is a root OR a failure reason and never a collapse of the two. (7) NOTHING BUILDS A TRIAGE REQUEST FROM THE STORE, AND NO REMAINING TASK OWNS IT. The three version dimensions a request records that nothing reads out of the engine are `enrichment_snapshot_version`, `normalization_snapshot_version` and `aggregation_version`; `helena.versions.AGGREGATION_VERSION_VIEW` is a starting point for the third. See the first `deferred` entry — this is the gap most likely to surprise task 52. (8) `docs/decisions/0032-deterministic-routing.md` §6 is the answer to 'what would reverse the orchestration choice': a measured need for resumability (and note that the compatible version is a checkpoint as typed rows in the single store keyed by (context reference, context version, trigger), NOT a framework's backend), human-in-the-loop interrupts (which need a surface the first version does not have), and a third agent whose SELECTION is a judgement rather than a value the code already has — a third branch is still an `if`. `tests/test_orchestration.py` holds the absence of every graph framework, workflow engine and checkpoint store as three tests, including the standard library's own file-backed ones.
